do you have any examples of applications that use this?

I have seen no application using those symlinks. Because devices mostly have FRUs (e.g NVME), EM will probe bus numbers for them without them having to do anything to be aware of the bus nums. Otherwise, platforms will choose to config muxes in dts so the channel nums can be statically alias. I think therefore, there's currently no service utilizing the symlinks. But the commit (https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/commit/286babcaa540a930126aa73b1ceccbca799d895c) supporting this said that those are to aid other applications. I'm planning to let dbus-sensors i2c sensor daemons use this. From my example in the commit msg, nvmesensor will implement code to read the symlink.
Thanks for the explanation.

> https://hsdes.intel.com/resource/15014280559

Is there a FRU on your NVMe? Just want to understand the use case since most NVMe have FRU and can be used to detect presence.

NVMe drives might have FRU or not, depends on the drive plugged. Even when all having FRUs, the problem is that we can’t have the mapping between the drives with FRU vs physical slot index in the chassis. Then, for example to report Temp sensor on each drive, it’s hard to do.
With this support, we can probe Temp sensors on NVMe drivers via the knowledge about the physical slots on the chassis.
The advantage of FRU detection is that temperature sensors are only created when NVMe drives are actually plugged in. Is your system always have the drives installed?

As NVMEs are pluggable devices, I don't expect they are all plugged.
When no drive is plugged on a certain slot, no /sys/class/hwmon is created so no Temp sensor is created.

Hi @Zhikui, sorry for late response due to our holiday. Our NVMEs don't always have FRU as we haven't been able to convince within our company and our HW team to cover that requirement. Aside from NVME, there can be many other sensors and devices behind the mux which does not necessarily have a FRU. If we want to config the mux in EM, then we also want a way to map the channel bus of the mux to the the i2c bus of the sensors. That's what motivates this patch.
Ack
Looks good to me, though I'm not all that familiar with how the mux channels are used. Others can weigh in.

Just want to clarify about the use of MuxChannel from this commit.
Currently we need to add I2C mux configuration from device tree like https://github.com/openbmc/linux/blob/8ae3366e3417677c299f548541e561324be4b536/arch/arm/boot/dts/aspeed/aspeed-bmc-ampere-mtjade.dts#L437.
When having this support, we will be no longer need to have this definition in device tree but just in entity-manager. Is it right, Chau?
Thanks anh @Thang. Right, although there's still many problems using mux config in EM but this is what this patch attempts.
Overall i think this is a nice feature to add.

Could this be rebased onto master? I have added CLs under the "add-muxchannel-object" topic to implement the MuxChannel object. The CL I have based on this one cannot pass verification without the rebase
Sure.
Waiting for the corresponding dbus-sensors reviews to get some traction

75497: Add I2CMux and I2CBus objects | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/75497

75503: Use I2CMux and I2CBus objects to get bus number | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/75503
Yes. But those are works from another company that are based on this new schema, together with the EM implementation in this relation chain. You can follow up those patches instead.

This is more of a question rather than a review:

It's  documented to not add new properties to the ```Aggregate``` schema.

Line 5, in "description"

```
Don't add additional properties to this schema. Consult README.schema for instructions on adding new Exposes element sub-schema.
```

Is there something that I'm missing here?

Hi @alexander.hansen@9elements.com, thanks for pointing out. I moved "MuxChannel" into the subschemas of each sensor (the impact list is added to the commit msg). However, I still temporarily put one "MuxChannel" property in "Aggregate" until your extract patches are fully merged.

FYI, I added a [patch](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/79539/1) to this relation chain to remove Bus/Address from ADC because they are redundant. My apology that we Ampere accidentally put them in our config which must have been part of the reason you added them to ADC subschema.

Thanks for helping to clean up the schemas!

I think it will be easier and faster to merge since you are removing the redundant property and only one config is affected (which is owned by ampere)

Ok, good to note!

> Other applications can then form the device file path from these
properties, and read the symbolic link to know the needed i2c bus.

So, if this replaces the need for ```Bus``` property, we probably need to have ```oneOf``` logic in all schemas which use the ```MuxChannel``` to prevent both being configured in the same record.

I think you already did this for some of the other schemas.

> So, if this replaces the need for Bus property, we probably need to have oneOf logic in all schemas which use the MuxChannel to prevent both being configured in the same record.

That would require more logics to the config to achieve that, even if/else might be involved I think. Should we pursuit that?

> I think you already did this for some of the other schemas.

I just added the logic that requires only one of Bus or MuxChannel for sensor types that have "Bus" in "required". For other types that don't require Bus, I simply added MuxChannel to the list.

> That would require more logics to the config to achieve that, even if/else might be involved I think. Should we pursuit that?

If it's possible to express in the schema, i think we should do that.

It can help to reduce the time needed to produce valid configuration 👍


For how to go about this, can either express it in this schema or simply split the schema and have one with ```Bus``` and one with ```MuxChannel```.

If it has to be split and cannot be done otherwise then it probably needs to go into its own file to prevent fragmentation / bitrot.
Updated. It's a bit tricky in the logic but brief and concise for this requirement. Please help read the commit message where I explain the logic.
